title: Cybersecurity Observatory
tagline: Network-attack datasets for AI security, all in one place.
lead: A curated catalogue of network-traffic datasets for AI-based cybersecurity: what each dataset contains, where it is distributed and which paper introduced it.
feature_title: A curated catalogue of network-attack datasets for AI
feature_text: Traffic datasets for intrusion detection, malware and C2 analysis and anomaly detection, linked to their original papers and distribution sources. Researchers can also submit new datasets.
about: Many datasets are used to evaluate AI methods for intrusion detection, malware and command-and-control analysis, and anomaly detection, but the same dataset name often refers to different releases, captures and derived feature tables.
The Observatory records every dataset at the level of the **release and its distributed artifacts**, and links it to its original publication and distribution source.
eligibility: A dataset is included when it distributes recorded network communications (packet captures, flow records, wireless frames, CAN or V2X messages, protocol logs) or features demonstrably derived from them, whatever the security task. Host-only telemetry, malware binaries and sensor time series without a network-traffic component are not eligible on their own.

units.name: Family
units.text: A named line of related collections (e.g. the Stratosphere Malware Capture Facility).

units.name: Release
units.text: A documented distribution at a given stage (e.g. IoT-23 v1).

units.name: Capture
units.text: A single acquisition event or scenario inside a release.

units.name: Artifact
units.text: A file or package actually delivered to researchers (full PCAP, flow-only archive, CSV).

records.name: CICIDS2017
records.notes: Landing page documents PCAP and derived CSV flows; equivalence between public CSV versions and the packets used to derive them is unverified.

records.name: UNSW-NB15
records.notes: Official distribution documented (PCAP, Argus/Bro, CSV); whether every derivative keeps the original packet information needs a file audit.

records.name: CTU-13
records.notes: Scenario-level provenance: capture identity matters when building train/test splits; PCAP coverage differs across releases.

records.name: BoT-IoT

paper.cite: Koroniotis et al., Future Generation Computer Systems 2019

records.notes: The full collection and the ~5% extraction are described separately: class proportions measured on the subset must not be attributed to the full dataset.

records.name: ToN-IoT
records.notes: Mixed-modality family: only the network-traffic components are eligible; host and telemetry records are excluded.

records.name: IoT-23
records.notes: 20 malicious and 3 benign captures; the full archive (~21 GB, PCAP + Zeek labels) and the flow-only archive (~8.8 GB) are different representations, not separate datasets. v1 and v2 must not be mixed.

records.name: CICIoT2023
records.notes: Check per-attack capture and the equivalence between PCAP and CSV releases.

records.name: HCRL Car-Hacking
records.notes: CAN-frame records, not Ethernet/IP packets; the originating collection paper is unconfirmed.

records.name: VeReMi

paper.cite: van der Heijden, Lukaseder & Kargl, SecureComm 2018

records.notes: Simulated V2X message logs for misbehavior detection, not IP packet captures.

records.name: N-BaIoT

paper.cite: Meidan et al., IEEE Pervasive Computing 2018

records.notes: Device-level leakage: validate on unseen devices.

records.name: SWaT
records.notes: Access on request. Process-only releases (sensor/actuator CSV) are not traffic-eligible; only releases with network captures qualify.

records.name: DNP3 Intrusion Detection Dataset
records.notes: Archive identified; representation to be inspected on acquisition.

records.name: HIKARI-2021
records.notes: Benign traffic plus encrypted synthetic attack traffic; not operational attacks.

records.name: USTC-TFC2016
records.task: Malware family and application traffic classification
records.notes: Malware and benign PCAP files are publicly enumerated; capture provenance and independence from CTU collections are unconfirmed.

records.name: CIC-DDoS2019
records.task: DDoS detection and attack family classification

records.name: CIC-AAGM2017
records.task: Android network malware and adware classification

records.name: CIC-YNU-IoTMal2026
records.task: IoT malware behavior and network classification

records.name: AWID

paper.cite: Kolias et al., IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials 2016

records.notes: 802.11 frame-level evidence: MAC-layer semantics are not equivalent to an IP-flow table.

records.name: MAWI samplepoint-F
records.notes: Long-term backbone packet traces; labels are not implicit and annotation availability differs from packet availability.

records.name: VAST Challenge 2012
data: Snort, firewall logs derived from traffic

records.name: NSL-KDD
records.notes: Legacy benchmark derived from KDD Cup 1999; redundancy and benchmark distortion are documented.

records.name: PDMFC Shennina HPing Nmap DDoS PCAPs
Kitsune Network Attack Dataset
records.task: IoT botnet and network attack detection
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Nine attacks: reconnaissance, man-in-the-middle, DoS and Mirai botnet.

records.name: InSDN
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. DoS, DDoS, brute force, web attacks, exploitation, probing and botnet. Licence CC BY-NC 4.0.

records.name: LITNET-2020
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Real academic network, 85 flow features, 12 attack types.

records.name: UWF-ZeekData22
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Zeek logs labelled with MITRE ATT&CK tactics. The labelled PCAPs use a custom binary format.

records.name: WUSTL-IIoT-2021

paper.cite: Zolanvari et al., IEEE Internet of Things Journal 2019

records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. DoS, reconnaissance, command injection and backdoor. Same group as WUSTL-EHMS-2020.

records.name: MQTT-IoT-IDS2020
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Scans, SSH brute force and MQTT brute force. Dataset doi:10.21227/bhxy-ep04.

records.name: TII-SSRC-23
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. DDoS, brute force, Mirai and information gathering.

records.name: ROAD (ORNL)
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Real fuzzing, fabrication and masquerade attacks on one vehicle. The link is the ORNL publication page.

records.name: SynCAN
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Synthetic signal-level CAN data with five attack types. The repository is archived (2023).

records.name: CICEVSE2024
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Reconnaissance and DoS (network), backdoor and cryptojacking (host).

records.name: CICAPT-IIoT2024
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. APT29-like campaign: more than 20 techniques in eight tactics.

records.name: X-IIoTID

paper.cite: Al-Hawawreh, Sitnikova, Aboutorab, IEEE Internet of Things Journal 2022

records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Multi-view features; also published on Kaggle.

records.name: CAIDA DDoS Attack 2007
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. One hour of a real DDoS attack (4 August 2007), about 21 GB uncompressed. Academic access on request.

records.name: ISCX Botnet 2014
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. Merges traffic of ISOT, ISCX 2012 and CTU-13 (already in the catalogue): not an independent acquisition.

records.name: LYCOS-IDS2017
records.notes: Found online on 2026-10-20, not in the reference list. CICIDS2017 traffic with the flows extracted again by a corrected tool.
